extracted.intended_audience: journalists around the world covering COVID-19
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and description of a multilingual online hub of self-directed courses, webinars, briefings and resources designed to help journalists cover the COVID-19 pandemic; describes features, content types, partners and regional briefings. Useful for journalists seeking training and reference materials on pandemic reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The hub itself is available in English, Spanish and Portuguese, and the resources and courses are translated into a growing number of languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can filter resources by language; the hub's multilingual design is emphasized as a core feature to facilitate access for journalists worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource types offered
rubrics_metrics.description: The online hub features self-directed courses, webinars, briefings and other resources in 13 languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include a mix of learning formats (self-paced courses, webinars, briefings) to accommodate different learning preferences and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and filter functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: At the top of the hub, users can search for self-directed courses and webinars by keyword, and filter by language or resource type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and filters are provided to help journalists quickly find relevant courses or resources by topic, language, or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage topics
rubrics_metrics.description: These COVID-19 courses and webinars cover topics like vaccines, variants, medications and disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hub targets substantive topical areas critical to pandemic reporting, suggesting relevance for journalists seeking topic-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-directed course structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The self-directed courses are divided into modules that feature video presentations and transcripts, as well as readings and links to other resources. They can be taken at any time and on the user’s own schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course design emphasizes modularity, multimedia (video + transcripts), supplemental readings/links, and on-demand access for working journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional briefings with best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Special briefings written by science and health journalists offer best practices and insights on covering COVID-19 in five different regions of the Global South: Latin America and the Caribbean, North Africa and the Middle East, West Africa, Eastern Africa, and Southern Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefings are region-specific, authored by specialists, and filterable by language; they are presented as practical, context-aware guidance for reporters in those regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative partnerships and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The hub was launched by the Knight Center in partnership with UNESCO and funded by the European Union; the Knight Center's Journalism Courses program has worked with UN agencies including UNESCO, UNDP, and WHO to produce resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships with UNESCO, UNDP, WHO and funding from EU/WHO are cited as indicators of credibility and institutional backing for the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated list of external authoritative resources
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bottom of the page, users will find a list of resources from organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO), Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), Dart Center, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hub aggregates and links to established organizations, offering reporters vetted external references and tools relevant to pandemic coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing updates and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: This hub is an ongoing project and will be updated with more resources as the Knight Center continues its efforts to help journalists around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content is presented as dynamic and expandable, implying the hub should be revisited periodically for new or updated materials.
